description: The PICTURE character-string length bound (§2023:13.18.40.3 SR4: 63 characters in the 2023 text) is 30 below COBOL-2002 - a RELAXATION, so a 31-to-50-character character-string-1 compiles at 2002 and later and is rejected at COBOL-85 with COBOL2146 (also under --permissive: a length error, not a removed construct), the word-length row's posture. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965; VCR row 7.46): the 1985 text reads 'The maximum number of characters allowed in the character-string is 30' (§1985:VI.5.9.3 SR4); the 2002 text's 13.16.38.2 SR4 reads 'The maximum number of characters allowed in character-string-1 is 50' and its Annex F.2 item 94 records 'The maximum number of characters that may be specified in a picture character-string is increased from 30 to 50'; 2014 raises the bound to 63 (§2014:13.18.40.2 SR4; §2014:E.3 item 19), the edge of row picture-string-63-2014. ONE bound, PictureAnalyzer.MaxStringLength(edition), read by Analyze's prologue (kb/Work PB4304).
display: a PICTURE character-string longer than 30 characters
rule1985: §1985:VI.5.9.3 SR4 (at most 30 characters in the PICTURE character-string)
vcr: VCR row 7.46 (PICTURE character-string bound 30 -> 50 at 2002); kb/Work PB4304
